comment: Runs 001-005 (review account, cites P-0037): two A at rest, tracker, sample_dt 0.02, all in domain (A, N = 2, r0 in [3.5, 9], predict() raises no ValueError). Initial separations 3.51 (001, 0.01 inside the 3.5 edge, T 1.0), 3.90 (002, diagonal, T 1.25), 4.25 (003, T 1.5), 4.75 (004, diagonal, T 2.0), 8.98 (005, 0.02 inside the 9 edge, T 4.0). RMSE/L of predict() against each run (RMS over samples, particles and coordinates, divided by L = 10): 0.00485, 0.00496, 0.00521, 0.00513, 0.00510. All five are below the bar 3 x 0.007 = 0.021, and none reaches contact (the paper's own window check passed on all five). Verdict is replicated on the stated bound. Limits: the judged metric sits at the tracker noise floor (about 0.005 for a correct model), so these runs test the bound and the window rule, not the shape of the linear 3.5-to-5 segment. From my own per-run K fits (not judged), the measured K at 3.5 and 4.5 is about 1.3 to 3 percent above the paper's linear fill; this is not a claim. Lab-keystone may wish to say whether the fill was chosen or measured.
